overview.body: This is an ENHANCE unit: lists take over! Your menus and the gate run from parallel lists instead of long if chains, and the game keeps a list of every city and hazard on the trip, shows them in the report, and saves them with the game.

mentorQuote.quote: Every time you copy a block and change one word, you're writing data as code. Lists let you write the data once and the code once. This week the game gets shorter and does more.

objectives: Move save and load into your library
Store each city's destinations in parallel lists, and show any menu with one function
Look up the gate's destination by index, from 1-based choices to 0-based positions
Build lists with append(), and sort a copy() for the report
Save lists of any length to a file, with a marker line, and read them back
overview.keyConceptsText: Chapter 7: lists, indexing, for loops over lists, append(), len(), sort(), copying lists, and reading and writing lists in files
overview.textbookReference: Starting Out with Python, 6th Edition by Tony Gaddis, Chapter 7. The for loop is from Chapter 4; this lab is the first to use it.

content.body: Lab 3.2 starts by tidying up. SAVE_FILE, save_game(), and load_game() move out of your game and into function_library.py, next to your other reusable functions. The game plays exactly as before.

Your game file should hold the game. Saving and loading are tools the game uses, like rolling the die or checking a menu choice, and tools live in the library. Moving them doesn't change what they do. It changes how the game reaches them: save_game() becomes function_library.save_game(). This lab adds four more library functions, all built on lists, so the library is where the work is.

content.body: One menu instead of two. Each city's destinations become two parallel lists, one of names and one of distances, and a single library function shows the menu for whichever city you're in.

Right now the game has a block of print() lines for San Antonio and another for Houston. A list holds many values under one name, and destinations[0] is the first one. Parallel lists keep related values at the same position: SA_DESTINATIONS[1] is Houston, and SA_DISTANCES[1] is the 200 miles to it. A for loop over range(len(destinations)) visits every position once, so display_destinations() prints any city's menu, however many choices it has. It returns that number, so the prompt can say Choice (1-3): or Choice (1-2): by itself.

content.quote: Two menus that print the same way is one menu waiting to happen. Put the data in lists, write the printing once, and adding a city later means adding two lines of data, not another copy of the menu. That's the whole reason lists exist.

    Returns:

def display_destinations(city, destinations, distances):
    """
    Show the numbered destination menu for a city.

    Args:
        city (str): The city the player is in
        destinations (list): The cities you can travel to
        distances (list): The miles to each one, in the same order

        print(f'  {i + 1}. {destinations[i]} - {distances[i]} miles')
    return len(destinations)

content.body: The gate without its long if/elif chains. Two library functions look up where you're going: one for HEADS, the choice you made, and one for TAILS, any other city on the menu.

The menu number is a position in the list, counting from 1, and list positions count from 0, so choice 1 is destinations[0]. get_destination() does that subtraction once. For TAILS, get_redirect() builds two new lists without the city you wanted, then picks a random position in them. That replaces Lab 3.1's redirect and every branch under it, for San Antonio and Houston alike. The cities TAILS sends you to are the same as before.

content.quote: TAILS used to be twenty lines I had to test one branch at a time. Now it's one function, and I can test it by pinning one number. index 0 is the first city that's left after yours comes out; index 1 is the second. Pin it, run it, check the city. Done.

items: In function_library.py, under display_destinations(), add the two functions, with two empty lines between each:

content.code:
def get_destination(destinations, distances, choice):
    """
    Look up the destination for a menu choice.

    Args:
        destinations (list): The cities on the menu
        distances (list): The miles to each one, in the same order
        choice (int): The menu number the player chose, from 1

    Returns:
        tuple: The destination and its distance
    """
    index = choice - 1
    return destinations[index], distances[index]


def get_redirect(destinations, distances, avoid):
    """
    Pick a random destination other than the one the player wanted.

    Args:
        destinations (list): The cities on the menu
        distances (list): The miles to each one, in the same order
        avoid (str): The destination the player wanted

    Returns:
        tuple: Another destination and its distance
    """
    cities = []
    miles = []
    for i in range(len(destinations)):
        if destinations[i] != avoid:
            cities.append(destinations[i])
            miles.append(distances[i])
    index = random.randint(0, len(cities) - 1)
    return cities[index], miles[index]

content.body: A save file that remembers the whole trip. After the nine values, savegame.txt lists the route, then a marker line, then the hazards. Loading reads them all back, and a damaged save file can't crash the game.

A list can be any length, so the file can't say "line 10 is the route." A for loop writes one city per line, then a marker line, ---LISTS_END---, says where the route stops and the hazards start. Reading is the same in reverse: a while loop reads cities until it reaches the marker, and another reads hazards until readline() returns '', the end of the file. If a number line holds something int() can't read, Python raises ValueError; catching it with FileNotFoundError gives the player the same friendly message as a missing file.

def save_game(player_name, current_city, total_miles, total_turns,
              total_hazards, total_escaped, games_played,
              session_miles, session_hazards, visited_cities,
              hazards_list):
    """
    Save the game to SAVE_FILE: nine values, one on each line, then
    the route, a marker line, and the hazards.

    Args:
        player_name (str): The player's name
        current_city (str): Where the player is now
        total_miles (int): Miles so far this game
        total_turns (int): Turns so far this game
        total_hazards (int): Hazards faced so far this game
        total_escaped (int): Hazards escaped so far this game
        games_played (int): Games finished this session
        session_miles (int): Miles in the finished games
        session_hazards (int): Hazards in the finished games
        visited_cities (list): Every city this game, in order
        hazards_list (list): Every hazard this game, in order
    """
    outfile = open(SAVE_FILE, 'w')
    outfile.write(player_name + '\n')
    outfile.write(current_city + '\n')
    outfile.write(str(total_miles) + '\n')
    outfile.write(str(total_turns) + '\n')
    outfile.write(str(total_hazards) + '\n')
    outfile.write(str(total_escaped) + '\n')
    outfile.write(str(games_played) + '\n')
    outfile.write(str(session_miles) + '\n')
    outfile.write(str(session_hazards) + '\n')
    for city in visited_cities:
        outfile.write(city + '\n')
    outfile.write('---LISTS_END---\n')
    for hazard in hazards_list:
        outfile.write(hazard + '\n')
    outfile.close()
    print('Game saved!')

content.code:
def load_game():
    """
    Load the game from SAVE_FILE.

    Returns:
        tuple: The nine saved values, then the route and the hazards,
        in the order save_game() writes them, or None if there is no
        save file or it can't be read
    """
    try:
        infile = open(SAVE_FILE, 'r')
        player_name = infile.readline().rstrip('\n')
        current_city = infile.readline().rstrip('\n')
        total_miles = int(infile.readline().rstrip('\n'))
        total_turns = int(infile.readline().rstrip('\n'))
        total_hazards = int(infile.readline().rstrip('\n'))
        total_escaped = int(infile.readline().rstrip('\n'))
        games_played = int(infile.readline().rstrip('\n'))
        session_miles = int(infile.readline().rstrip('\n'))
        session_hazards = int(infile.readline().rstrip('\n'))

        # The route, up to the marker line
        visited_cities = []
        line = infile.readline().rstrip('\n')
        while line != '---LISTS_END---' and line != '':
            visited_cities.append(line)
            line = infile.readline().rstrip('\n')

        # The hazards, up to the end of the file
        hazards_list = []
        line = infile.readline().rstrip('\n')
        while line != '':
            hazards_list.append(line)
            line = infile.readline().rstrip('\n')

        infile.close()
        return (player_name, current_city, total_miles, total_turns,
                total_hazards, total_escaped, games_played,
                session_miles, session_hazards, visited_cities,
                hazards_list)
    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):
        return None
